newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-RIEDEL GETS OUT OF SICK BED TO CLINCH FOURTH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-RIEDEL GETS OUT OF SICK BED TO CLINCH FOURTH TITLE.

text.p: German Lars Riedel defied the debilitating effects of a throat infection on Sunday to clinch his fourth consecutive world discus title.
Riedel, 30, had been suffering from the effects of the infection all week and even three days ago had wondered whether he would be fit enough to defend his title.
"I realised I was not Superman," said Riedel. "I had a bad fever and was starting to think about pulling out.
"What made me even more miserable was the fact that I haven't been able to get hold of my wife on the phone."
Nevertheless, Riedel still managed to hold body and soul together long enough for him to unleash the two kgs discus out to 68.54 metres in the second round.
No one apart from Riedel has thrown further this year.
"After that throw I was sure the competition was all over and the fourth title was mine," Riedel added.
Only Ukrainian pole vaulter Sergei Bubka has won more world titles in one event.
Riedel believes he still has time to catch up and overhaul Bubka and his outstanding record of six victories.
"The world record is not important, world titles are," Riedal said. "I intend defending my title in Seville and staying around for many years after that."
He said he had gained inspiration from his compatriot and friend Juergen Schult.
Schult, 37, threw 66.14 for the bronze medal and has finished in the top six at all six World Championships.
Ironically Schult is still the holder of the world best of 74.08, set in 1986, despite the attentions of Riedel in recent years.
Riedel's nearest rival on the night acknowledged that the German giant is in a different league to the rest of the world's top discus throwers.
"I am the best in the world, after Lars Riedel. I was quite clear tonight we were all competing for second and third places," second-placed Virgilijus Alekna said.
The Lithuanian took the silver medal with his second round effort of 66.70.
